record.original_question: Clarify the relationship between flat virtual-knot theories and theories of doodles, including doodles with virtual crossings, and determine the resulting structures for cobordism, associated groups, and free-abelian cobordism classes of immersed surfaces without triple points.

evidence.quote: Virtuals and the Theory of Doodles: Compare flat theories of virtual knots with theories of doodles.
Cobordism of doodles is defined by an immersed surface without triple points. Cobordism classes represent elements of a free abelian group.
For example there is no reason not to have virtual crossings as well as flat crossings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A flat virtual knot is an equivalence class of 4-valent planar diagrams whose crossings are of two types — flat (transverse, with no over/under information) and virtual (drawn with a small circle) — modulo the flat versions of the generalized Reidemeister moves: the three classical Reidemeister moves performed with flat crossings, the three virtual Reidemeister moves performed with virtual crossings, and the mixed "detour" move that allows an arc containing only virtual crossings to be replaced by any other such arc with the same endpoints.

A doodle is a collection of closed curves immersed in the 2-sphere (or, more generally, in a closed oriented surface) having only transverse double points and no triple points, considered up to the doodle Reidemeister-type moves that exclude the move corresponding to passing one strand across a double point of two others (so triple points are forbidden during isotopy). A cobordism between two doodles is an immersed orientable surface in (surface)×[0,1] whose singular set consists only of double-point curves, with no triple points; the set of cobordism classes of doodles forms a free abelian group under disjoint union.

Formulate and develop a precise correspondence between flat virtual knot theory and the theory of doodles in the following sense:

(a) Define a category of "virtual doodles" by allowing diagrams to contain both flat (double-point) crossings and virtual crossings, together with appropriate Reidemeister-type and detour moves, and determine the precise relationship (functor, equivalence, or embedding) between this category and the category of flat virtual knots.

(b) Define cobordism of virtual doodles via immersed surfaces without triple points in the appropriate thickened surface, and determine the resulting cobordism group; in particular, decide whether the cobordism classes form a free abelian group as in the classical doodle case, and compute or characterize this group.

(c) Determine the analogue, in this combined setting, of the group naturally associated to a doodle (the "doodle group", playing a role analogous to the knot group, with twin groups replacing braid groups), and describe its relationship to the groups associated with flat virtual knots.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of clarifying the relationship between flat virtual knot theory and the theory of doodles (including the cobordism group of immersed surfaces without triple points and associated groups) appears as an open research direction. While there has been substantial subsequent work on virtual knot cobordism, doodles, twin groups, and related invariants (e.g. Manturov's free-group valued invariant of free knots, Kauffman's virtual knot cobordism), no source verifies a complete resolution of the proposed comparison and structure-determination program.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Virtual Knot Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Compare flat theories of virtual knots with theories of doodles. Cobordism of doodles is defined by an immersed surface without triple points. Cobordism classes represent elements of a free abelian group.
status_evidence.claim: The comparison is posed as an unsolved problem.

status_evidence.title: A free-group valued invariant of free knots (Manturov)
status_evidence.snippet: Invariants of free/flat knots developed using free-group valued constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops invariants of flat virtual knots but does not complete the doodle comparison.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Cobordism (Kauffman)
status_evidence.snippet: Cobordism and concordance of virtual knots and links is developed as a generalization of classical knot cobordism.
status_evidence.claim: Virtual knot cobordism is developed but the doodle/triple-point free abelian cobordism comparison is not fully resolved.
